caption: A serving cart carrying a tray of full water glasses is pushed forward and stopped short, and the water sloshes forward and spills.

sa.check: A serving cart carries a tray of full water glasses.
The cart is pushed forward and then stopped short.
Several glasses stand on the tray rather than a single one.
The cart stops first, then the slosh, then the spill.

pc.expect: The water surfaces lie level while the cart rolls steadily and surge at the moment it is stopped.
pc.fail: The water sloshes while the cart is rolling at a steady speed; or it surges with no stop visible; or it keeps sloshing long after the cart is still.

pc.expect: The surge carries the water toward the front of the cart, the way it was moving, and over the forward rims.
pc.fail: The water surges toward the back of the cart when it stops; or it climbs evenly around every rim; or it lifts straight up out of the glasses.

pc.expect: The water tilts as one connected surface, slops over the rim and runs down the outside of the glass onto the tray.
pc.fail: A water surface stays flat and rigid while its glass is plainly lurching; or water leaves a glass as a solid lump that keeps its shape; or the spill gathers into balls that roll off the tray.

pc.expect: Spilled water runs down the outsides of the glasses and pools on the tray, dripping over its edge.
pc.fail: Spilled water climbs the outside of a glass; or a spill floats above the tray; or the puddle gathers on top of a glass.

pc.expect: The glasses keep their number and shape and water leaves them only over the rim.
pc.fail: A glass vanishes or a new one appears on the tray; or water passes through the wall of a glass; or a glass merges with the tray; or the water level in a glass rises while it is spilling.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The glasses, the tray and the cart keep their colour and arrangement apart from the slosh.
pc.fail: The tray changes colour; or the glasses change size or pattern; or the cart's shelves rearrange between frames.
